topic.name: Combining Graph Transformations: Three or More Operations

question.text:
The graph of $y=7f(2x-2)+5,$ can be obtained from the graph of $y=f(x)$ by applying some of the following transformations:

  • $(\textrm{T}1)$ - Translate up by $5$ units

  • $(\textrm{T}2)$ - Stretch by a scale factor of $7$ parallel to the $y$-axis

  • $(\textrm{T}3)$ - Translate right by $1$ unit

  • $(\textrm{T}4)$ - Stretch by a scale factor of $0.5$ parallel to the $x$-axis

  • $(\textrm{T}5)$ - Translate right by $2$ units

Which of the following could be a possible ordering of the appropriate transformations?
question.explanation:
To perform transformations of functions with multiple operations, we must remember the following rule:

  1. First, we perform the transformations inside the argument of $f.$ We first carry out horizontal stretches, followed by horizontal translations.

  2. Then, we perform the transformations outside the argument of $f.$ We first carry out vertical stretches, followed by vertical translations.

First, let's factor out the coefficient next to the $x$ inside the function:

\[ y=7f(2x-2)+5 =7f\big(2(x-1)\big)+5 \]

To get $y=7f\big(2(x-1)\big)+5,$ we could apply the following steps:

  • Take the curve $y=f(x).$

  • Apply transformation $(\textrm{T}4).$ Stretch $y=f(x)$ by a scale factor of $\dfrac{1}{2}=0.5$ parallel to the $x$-axis to get the graph of \[ y=f(2x).\]

  • Apply transformation $(\textrm{T}3).$ Translate $y=f(2x)$ right by $1$ unit to get the graph of \[ y=f\big(2(x-1)\big). \]

  • Apply transformation $(\textrm{T}2).$ Stretch $y=f\big(2(x-1)\big)$ by a scale factor of $7$ parallel to the $y$-axis to get the graph of \[ y=7f\big(2(x-1)\big). \]

  • Apply transformation $(\textrm{T}1).$ Translate $y=7f\big(2(x-1)\big)$ up by $5$ units to get the graph of \[ y=7f\big(2(x-1)\big)+5. \]

Therefore, a possible order of transformations is

$\qquad$ $(\textrm{T}4) \to (\textrm{T}3) \to (\textrm{T}2) \to (\textrm{T}1).$

question.text:
The graph of $y=4f(2x)-3,$ can be obtained from the graph of $y=f(x)$ by applying some of the following transformations:

  • $(\textrm{T}1)$ - Translate up by $3$ units

  • $(\textrm{T}2)$ - Stretch by a scale factor of $4$ parallel to the $y$-axis

  • $(\textrm{T}3)$ - Translate down by $3$ units

  • $(\textrm{T}4)$ - Stretch by a scale factor of $0.5$ parallel to the $x$-axis

Which of the following could be a possible ordering of the appropriate transformations?
question.explanation:
To perform transformations of functions with multiple operations, we must remember the following rule:

  1. First, we perform the transformations inside the argument of $f.$ We first carry out horizontal stretches, followed by horizontal translations.

  2. Then, we perform the transformations outside the argument of $f.$ We first carry out vertical stretches, followed by vertical translations.

To get $y=4f\big(2x\big)-3,$ we could apply the following steps:

  • Take the curve $y=f(x).$

  • Apply transformation $(\textrm{T}4).$ Stretch $y=f(x)$ by a scale factor of $\dfrac{1}{2}=0.5$ parallel to the $x$-axis to get the graph of \[ y=f(2x).\]

  • Apply transformation $(\textrm{T}2).$ Stretch $y=f\big(2x\big)$ by a scale factor of $4$ parallel to the $y$-axis to get the graph of \[ y=4f\big(2x\big). \]

  • Apply transformation $(\textrm{T}3).$ Translate $y=4f\big(2x\big)$ down by $3$ units to get the graph of \[ y=4f\big(2x\big)-3. \]

Therefore, a possible order of transformations is

$\qquad$ $(\textrm{T}4) \to (\textrm{T}2) \to (\textrm{T}3).$

example.title: Determining the Correct Order of Transformations Given a Transformed Function Expression

question.text:
The graph of $y=3f\left(5x-15\right),$ can be obtained from the graph of $y=f(x)$ by applying some of the following transformations:

  • $(\textrm{T}1)$ - Stretch by a scale factor of $3$ parallel to the $y$-axis

  • $(\textrm{T}2)$ - Stretch by a scale factor of $0.2$ parallel to the $x$-axis

  • $(\textrm{T}3)$ - Stretch by a scale factor of $5$ parallel to the $x$-axis

  • $(\textrm{T}4)$ - Translate right by $3$ units

Which of the following could be a possible ordering of the appropriate transformations?
question.explanation:
To perform transformations of functions with multiple operations, we must remember the following rule:

  1. First, we perform the transformations inside the argument of $f.$ We first carry out horizontal stretches, followed by horizontal translations.

  2. Then, we perform the transformations outside the argument of $f.$ We first carry out vertical stretches, followed by vertical translations.

First, let's factor out the coefficient next to the $x$ inside the function:

\[ y=3f\left(5x-15\right) = 3f\big(5(x-3)\big) \]

To get $y=3f\big(5(x-3)\big),$ we could apply the following steps:

  • Take the curve $y=f(x).$

  • Apply transformation $(\textrm{T}2).$ Stretch $y=f(x)$ by a scale factor of $\dfrac15=0.2$ parallel to the $x$-axis to get the graph of \[ y=f(5x).\]

  • Apply transformation $(\textrm{T}4).$ Translate $y=f(5x)$ right by $3$ units to get the graph of \[ y=f\big(5(x-3)\big).\]

  • Apply transformation $(\textrm{T}1).$ Stretch $y=f\big(5(x-3)\big)$ by a scale factor of $3$ parallel to the $y$-axis to get the graph of \[ y=3f\big(5(x-3)\big). \]

Therefore, a possible order of transformations is

$\qquad$ $(\textrm{T}2) \to (\textrm{T}4) \to (\textrm{T}1).$
